Samir — thanks, good constraints. Drafting the runbook below so procurement can attach it to the MAP. This is intended to be the canonical source for the pilot acceptance gate.

Workload definition (what we will run):
- Model: rwdn-v2-large (same family as demo; exact commit: rwdn-v2-large@2027-02-14)
- Prompt mix: 80% short (<=64 tokens), 20% long (>=512 tokens) — sampled from Novamed sanitized corpus
- Sequence lengths: short median 48, long median 640 (pad to 1024 where needed)
- Traffic shape: daytime burst profile (8am-6pm PT); peak QPS target 120, sustained QPS 40
- Concurrent requests: ramp to 60 concurrent sessions (concurrency = 60)

Success criteria / SLOs (pass = all must be met):
- Time to first token (TTFT): p90 <= 120ms, p95 <= 180ms
- Latency per token: p95 <= 25ms per token for short sequences
- End-to-end response latency (full response): p95 <= 1.2s for short prompts, p95 <= 5s for long prompts
- Throughput: sustain 40 QPS for 2 hours without degradation; handle 120 QPS transiently with graceful degradation
- Error rate: API error rate < 0.1% (5xx/timeout) during runs

Instrumentation & data:
- Test harness: Redwood perf harness (kvm-based collectors) + OpenTelemetry traces; client load generator: rwdn-load v0.9
- Datasets: sanitized dev corpus (Novamed-provided) + canonical stress cases from Redwood QA
- Metrics to collect: TTFT, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, CPU, network, mem, error counts

Run plan & schedule:
- Baseline run (single config): 2027-03-18 09:00-11:00 PT — validate harness and dataset
- Validation run (production config): 2027-03-19 09:00-13:00 PT — sustained 2-hour window with 40 QPS and 60 concurrency ramp
- Spike test: 2027-03-20 11:00-12:00 PT — transient bursts up to 120 QPS (1-3 minute bursts)

Deliverables:
- Run artifacts: perf-snapshot-MAP.csv (aggregates + raw traces), live dashboard link, runbook PDF (attached)
- Acceptance decision sign-off template for procurement

Questions / open items for Novamed:
1) Confirm sanitized dataset delivery timeline (we need final set by 2027-03-17 12:00 PT)
2) Any additional regional constraints (we plan to run in us-west-2 unless you request eu)

If this looks good I will schedule the baseline run and loop in infra for the validation window.

—Irene

Adding some execution detail from the infra side — quick checklist and clarifications so runs are reproducible: 

Execution checklist (infra / test engineering):
- Isolation: run in dedicated Dedicated pool (pinned GPUs) to avoid noisy neighbors — reserved instance group rdw-dedicated-novamed-1
- Model variants: run baseline on fp16, and a second pass using 4-bit quantized variant (q4f8) to compare cost/latency tradeoffs
- Warm cache policy: 15-minute warm-up with 10k prefix-cache items representative of Novamed corpus
- Data sampling: we will seed the generator with your 1:5 short:long distribution; please confirm the sample ID list
- Observability: enable token-level traces for the 1st and 100th request per minute to correlate KV cache hits

Acceptance guardrails: if p95 TTFT exceeds 200ms in baseline (fp16) run we abort and capture heap/host dumps for RCA. For quantized runs we expect modest TTFT improvement but must validate model output quality in parallel evals (QA team).

Irene — I will provision the dedicated pool and post the access details here once ready. Planning note: run artifacts (~120MB compressed) will be uploaded to the Novamed shared Drive link in related_links.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Perf & Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Team — completed the validation run this morning (attached snapshot). Quick summary vs acceptance gates: 

Summary (validation run 2027-03-19 09:00-11:30 PT):
- Baseline (fp16): sustained 45 QPS for 2 hours, concurrency target 60
  - TTFT: p90 = 98ms, p95 = 145ms 
  - End-to-end short p95 = 1.05s; long p95 = 4.6s
  - Error rate: 0.03% (timeouts during 1 transient spike)
- Quantized (q4f8) quick pass: TTFT improved ~18% p95; however, output quality regression detected on 2 QA prompts (tracked separately)

Pass/fail: baseline fp16 run passes all acceptance gates. Quantized runs are promising for cost but require QA sign-off before using as the default in MAP.

Artifacts: perf-snapshot-MAP.csv attached (aggregates + per-request traces) and runbook updated in the shared link. We recorded GPU utilization (avg 86% during steady state).

Next steps proposed:
1) Novamed: confirm acceptance of baseline fp16 numbers as the MAP performance gate
2) Redwood: run a second quantized experiment with targeted prompts flagged by QA (to see if regressions are limited)
3) Schedule a 30-min sign-off call (options below)
